newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finance ministry may scrap planned NFI tax.
newsitem.headline: Polish finance ministry may scrap planned NFI tax.

text.p: Poland's finance minister Marek Belka may drop plans to levy tax on profits made through sales of firms by the country's National Investment Funds (NFI), if that is what parliament decides, he said on Friday.
Late last month the ministry said that from the start of 1998 the 15 NFIs would have to pay a 36 percent tax on gains they made from sales of companies in their portfolios.

But PAP news agency quoted Belka as saying in the city of Lodz that the tax was not "the automatic decision of the finance minister but the realisation of the will of the Sejm (lower house of parliament)."

Earlier this week Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz said he would ask Belka not to remove the exemption hitherto enjoyed by the NFIs, saying the tax would reduce their ability to invest in other firms in their portfolios.
The finance ministry has said its move was in line with the will of parliamentary committees which shaped the new income tax laws and rejected proposals to keep the NFI tax breaks.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in more than 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
